learned_operations: Classify the four public query semantics from either their public IDs or reusable action, recipient, and trigger language.
Recognize confidentiality agreements before treating a full-document scan as sufficient evidence of absence; unsupported documents return null.
Resolve short-range clause anaphora such as “the same” back to an exact Confidential Information passage while preserving every evidence item as an exact source substring.
Infer existential sharing permission from may-disclose language, need-to-know access restrictions, and explicit disclosure exceptions for a recipient subset.
Separate Receiving Party employees from affiliate employees and from staff belonging to the disclosing, originating, or other party.

Expand a locally defined Representative recipient only when the definition actually includes employees, while treating agents, advisers, consultants, contractors, affiliates, and similar recipients as third parties.
Preserve termination as a rule trigger: a return-or-destroy obligation can be entailed even when the document does not state that termination actually occurred.
Infer post-return retention only from a return/destruction clause containing an express retention, archival-copy, or equivalent exception; generic written-approval exceptions elsewhere are not used.
Compile permissions, obligations, prohibitions, scopes, triggers, exact quotes, and exception overrides into the supplied graph schema, then delegate native answer resolution to scope_answer.
Return native NotMentioned only after recognizing the document and completing a full scan for all four supported query families; parsing or source-classification failure remains null.
limitations: The procedure supports the four disclosed NDA query families, not arbitrary contractual questions.
It uses paragraph-local syntax plus bounded anaphora and may leave unusually remote cross-references, tables, malformed OCR, or deeply nested definitions unresolved.

Employee authorization through affiliates is deliberately not treated as authorization for the Receiving Party’s own employees unless a separate direct employee authorization or an applicable Representative definition is present.
Post-return retention requires explicit return/destruction context and retention language; it will not invent retention rights from a generic consent or amendment clause.

Semantic distinctions outside the public graph vocabulary—such as quantities beyond existential “some,” detailed purpose restrictions, notice periods, and choice of return versus destruction—are retained only as conditions or evidence and are not independently answered.
